items.title: Missing father and son found weak after three days in Terengganu forest without food
items.summary: JERTIH, Oct 17 — A father and son who went missing on Thursday while searching for medicinal roots in a forest near the La Hot Spring recreational area in Hulu Besut were found safe at noon today. Besut police chief Supt Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said the two were brought out of the forest at 2.45pm via the Lata Kolam Air Deru recreational area. Bernama reported earlier today that the father and son had gone missing after entering the forest to search for medicinal roots.

items.title: After another downpour, Lembah Subang resident asks minister to step in over recurring floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Flash floods hit several parts of the Klang Valley after heavy rain this afternoon, as a Lembah Subang resident raised concerns over recurring floods in the neighbourhood, alleging that an unfinished pedestrian walkway project may be obstructing nearby drains. Threads user _anuarlatif said in a post today. Another Threads user, amm.yusopp, also reported flooding in Kampung Melayu Subang.

items.title: Saifuddin warns of synthetic drugs that make users appear like 'zombies'
items.summary: MACHANG: The emergence of synthetic drugs that can drastically alter users' behaviour, making them appear like "zombies", is a growing concern, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said. Saifuddin said drug use patterns varied by region, with synthetic drugs more prevalent on the east coast, while drug abuse on the west coast involved a mixture of substances. However, he said synthetic drug use remained high nationwide, partly because the substances were more easily accessible.

items.title: Residents complain of recurring floods in Petaling Jaya, Subang
items.summary: In a post on Threads, user _anuarlatif said flooding frequently occurred in Taman Putra Damai, Lembah Subang, which the user attributed to blocked drains following construction work along the area's main road. The user said soil and construction materials left by the roadside appeared to have washed into the drains, obstructing water flow. Meanwhile, another Threads user, amm.yusopp, reported flooding in Kampung Melayu Subang.

items.title: Budget 2027: Islamic affairs gets RM3.1b, as minister outlines support for ‘pondok’ schools, imams and halal SMEs
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — The Madani Government has increased the allocation for religious affairs to RM3.1 billion under Budget 2027 to strengthen Islamic development, including support for religious education institutions and the welfare of religious personnel nationwide. “The Madani Government continues to place special emphasis on this agenda by allocating RM200 million for sekolah agama rakyat (community religious schools), tahfiz institutions and sekolah pondok (traditional Islamic boarding schools) registered with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim). Zulkifli said the government would also provide a special contribution of RM750 each to 70,000 religious personnel, including Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain (Kafa) teachers, takmir teachers, imams, bilals, tok siaks , nojas and marbuts , in recognition of their contributions to the community.

items.title: Saifuddin hands new identity card to 70-year-old Kelantan woman
items.summary: MACHANG: After years of carrying a damaged identity card that was barely legible, 70-year-old Minah Yacob was relieved to receive her new-generation MyKad. Handing Minah the card, Saifuddin said: "Congratulations. Here is your new identity card."

items.title: 1.2 million workers yet to join Lindung 24 Jam scheme
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Some 1.2 million workers who had previously opted not to contribute to the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) Lindung 24 Jam scheme have been urged to take up the protection following the announcement of an additional annual tax relief of RM150 under the 2027 Budget. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the incentive offered workers a good opportunity to resume contributions to ensure they had social security protection in the event of accidents outside working hours. He said the government understood public concerns over disposable income amid inflationary pressures driven by global factors, but social security protection must remain a priority.

items.title: Govt allocates RM3.1b under 2027 Budget for Islamic development
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Madani government has increased the allocation for religious affairs to RM3.1 billion under the 2027 Budget to strengthen Islamic development, including the empowerment of religious educational institutions and safeguarding the welfare of religious personnel nationwide. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said 85.4 per cent of the allocation was for operating expenditure, while the remaining 14.6 per cent was set aside for development expenditure. "The Madani government continues to place special emphasis on this agenda by allocating RM200 million for sekolah agama rakyat (community religious schools), tahfiz institutions and sekolah pondok (traditional Islamic boarding schools) registered with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim).

items.title: Stop dumping pet fish in lakes, govt warns as alien species wiping out natives in Ampang lake
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Alien fish account for 95 per cent of fish recorded in Tasik Ampang Hilir, posing a serious threat to the balance of Malaysia’s freshwater ecosystem. He warned that releasing pet fish into lakes, dams and public waterways when they grow too large or become difficult to care for could harm aquatic biodiversity and threaten the survival of local species. Isham said measures included increasing efforts to catch alien fish, releasing local fish fry to help restore the balance of fish populations and expanding public education to discourage people from releasing pet fish into public waters.

items.title: Penang’s RM420m link road to Silicon Island targets first bridge opening by 2028
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — A total of 202.3 hectares of land have been reclaimed at Silicon Island since reclamation works began in September 2023, marking progress in the development of Penang’s next economic growth hub as of October 2026. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the development was envisioned to complement the state’s semiconductor industry while attracting investments in advanced technology, research and development, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven innovation. In a separate statement, Silicon Island Development Sdn Bhd said the Silicon Island Experience Centre was now open to government agencies, investors, local communities and strategic partners to help them better understand the 931-hectare development.

items.title: MAIS denies claims that Nik Nazmi's khalwat case was a "frame-up"
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) has denied allegations that the action against former Setiawangsa member of parliament Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad by the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) over a khalwat (proximity) case was an act of persecution or a "frame-up". MAIS chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said JAIS acted based on an official complaint and in accordance with established legal procedures, without manipulating the situation to target any individual. Also present was Selangor Mufti Datuk Dr Anhar Opir.

items.title: Police seize 125 motorcycles in Op Samseng Jalanan in Kuala Terengganu
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: Police issued 447 summonses and seized 125 motorcycles during 'Op Samseng Jalanan 2026', a two-day operation conducted at two locations in Kuala Terengganu. District police chief assistant commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the action followed inspections on motorcycles believed to have been involved in the Gen-Y Event 2026 celebrations. He said the offences detected included missing side mirrors, failure to display a valid motor vehicle licence, expired motor vehicle licences, non-compliant number plates and modified motorcycle exhausts.

items.title: Selangor Islamic council denies Jais ‘frame-up’ claims in Nik Nazmi’s khalwat detention, says no one is above the law
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 17 — The Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) has denied allegations that the detention of former Setiawangsa MP Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad by the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) last Thursday over a khalwat case was an act of persecution or a “frame-up”. Mais chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said Jais had acted on an official complaint and followed established legal procedures, without manipulating the situation to target any individual. Jais stands for Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor, or the Selangor Islamic Religious Department.

items.title: Missing father, son found safe in Besut forest after 3 days
items.summary: JERTIH: A man and his son who went missing on Thursday while searching for medicinal roots in a forest near the La Hot Spring recreational area in Hulu Besut were found safe at noon today. The two men, Adam Adnan, 25, and his father Adnan Mohamad, 57, were found by a search and rescue (SAR) team at 12.40pm, about 3km from the operation's command post. Besut police chief superintendent Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said they were brought out of the forest at 2.45pm via the Lata Kolam Air Deru recreational area.

items.title: PHEB gives aid to families affected by Nepal-Tibet tragedy
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Hindu Endowments Board (PHEB) has given one-off financial aid to families affected by the Aug 26 Nepal-Tibet border tragedy. PHEB deputy chairman Senator Dr Lingeshwaran R. Arunasalam said four families from Penang were identified, with three accepting the RM5,000 assistance. Speaking at the aid handover ceremony, Lingeshwaran urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the federal government to consider similar one-off assistance for all affected Malaysian families nationwide.

items.title: From USJ to Shah Alam, flash floods disrupt Klang Valley roads after afternoon downpour
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Afternoon thunderstorms brought flash floods to several parts of the Klang Valley today, inundating roads and disrupting traffic in Selangor as authorities urged motorists to avoid affected areas. Social media posts reported flooding in USJ 1, USJ 7, Sunway, Ara Damansara, Kota Damansara, Kampung Melayu Subang, Kampung Baru Hicom and Shah Alam, with motorists warned to plan their journeys carefully. In Shah Alam, the city council warned of rising water levels near the traffic lights at i-City in Section 7 and Padang Jawa in Section 16, advising the public to drive cautiously and avoid affected roads if water levels continued to rise.

items.title: Disabled person rescued from flood-hit home in Seberang Prai
items.summary: SEBERANG PRAI: A person with disabilities was rescued after being trapped inside a flood-hit home in Mengkuang Titi. The incident occurred after flash floods inundated several areas in the Seberang Prai Tengah district at about 4pm. Members of the Seberang Prai Tengah Civil Defence Force (CDF) rescued the victim from the rising floodwaters.

items.title: Myanmar man held with 10 others attempting to leave country illegally
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A Myanmar man believed to be acting as a transporter was arrested with 10 fellow citizens during an Immigration Department raid at a hotel in Wakaf Che Yeh. Immigration Department deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said the group comprised six men and four women who were believed to be working in Johor Baru and Kuala Lumpur. In a separate operation at a construction site in Kubang Kerian, the Kelantan Immigration Department inspected 57 foreign workers and detained 55 on suspicion of various immigration offences, Lokman Effendi said.

items.title: GRS takes its election pitch to Kudat, with Hajiji eyeing 16 parliamentary seats
items.summary: “Cooperation and unity among GRS components as well as our partners in the State Unity Government is vital to ensure a decisive victory for GRS in the coming general election,” said Hajiji, who is GRS Chairman and PGRS President. Besides Hajiji’s keynote address, the six GRS Deputy Chairmen will deliver speeches. Both Members of Parliament lost in the State election in November last year to GRS candidates.­ — Daily Express * Editor’s note: GRS stands for Gabungan Rakyat Sabah; PGRS stands for Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah; PBS stands for Parti Bersatu Sabah; PCS stands for Parti Cinta Sabah; LDP stands for Liberal Democratic Party; PHRS stands for Parti Harapan Rakyat Sabah; Upko stands for United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation; and SMJ stands for Sabah Maju Jaya.

items.title: Sri Lanka suffers nationwide electricity blackout
items.summary: COLOMBO: Sri Lanka suffered a nationwide electricity blackout on Saturday after the national grid tripped, possibly because solar power generation exceeded consumption, officials said. State-run Electricity Distribution Lanka (EDL) said engineers were working to fix a fault affecting the entire grid and suspected excess solar power had caused the breakdown. The entire grid shut down in February 2025, when solar power generation exceeded consumption on a bright, sunny Sunday.

items.title: Sarawak polls could be as early as November, says state minister Abdul Karim
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 17 — Sarawak could hold its 13th state election as early as November, with the polling window extending to mid-December, said State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Dato Sri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah. Abdul Karim, who is also Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) information chief, said the timing would depend on when Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg dissolves the Sarawak Legislative Assembly. The Election Commission (EC) would then determine the polling date in accordance with the law, he said.

items.title: 25 monitoring stations record unhealthy air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 25 air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with Pasir Gudang in Johor recording the highest at 198. In Sabah, Sandakan recorded a reading of 157, while Tawau recorded 129. Another 42 monitoring stations recorded moderate air quality.

items.title: Pas has list of candidates ready for Melaka polls, says Hadi
items.summary: CYBERJAYA: Pas has prepared a list of potential candidates for the upcoming Melaka election, with the final selection to be decided by the party's central leadership. Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the list contained numerous names for consideration. "There are many candidates on the list.

items.title: Melaka polls: PKR to field experienced, young and women candidates, says Amirudin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to firm up its direction for the Melaka state election within a week, with candidate selection now in its final stages, coalition election strategy director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said today. Amirudin said allowing candidates to gain experience in less favourable constituencies could help build a longer-term plan for PKR and the wider coalition. Party secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh said Pakatan Harapan would contest more seats overall if PKR’s allocation remained at nine.

items.title: Motorists call for action over daily gridlock along Jalan Maarof
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists plying Jalan Maarof in Bangsar are calling on authorities to address severe daily traffic gridlocks affecting commutes into the commercial hub. Drivers said the stretch turns into a persistent bottleneck during peak hours, driven by heavy traffic merging from multiple directions into narrow two-lane roads. Personal driver Muhammad Naim, 35, said the area experiences congestion during morning, noon, and evening rush hours.

items.title: MOH officers killed in helicopter crash receive posthumous promotions
items.summary: The ministry honoured the healthcare staff who served with the Flying Doctor Service (PDU), whose promotions were approved by the Public Service Promotion Board (LKPPA) on Oct 13. The board cleared 6,724 officers from various service schemes under the ministry for acting appointments and promotions to the Senior Management Service (JUSA) and Grades 10 to 15, the ministry said in a statement. The approvals reflect the ministry's continued efforts to recognise officers' commitment, dedication and achievements in ensuring smooth operations and effective healthcare service delivery.

items.title: Home minister: 24-hour border watch, jetty demolitions to curb cross-border crime in Kelantan
items.summary: MACHANG, Oct 17 — Police are maintaining round-the-clock surveillance along all border routes in Kelantan to curb cross-border crime, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the directive had been issued to Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat to ensure continuous physical surveillance along the border. He said the investigation papers included witness statements and information gathered throughout the investigation.

items.title: Japan retracts mistaken magnitude 9.9 quake alert
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan's weather agency withdrew an erroneous alert for a magnitude 9.9 earthquake minutes after issuing it, apologising for a warning that disrupted transport. The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) had initially warned on Friday that a magnitude 9.9 earthquake had occurred near the Kuril Islands, known in Japan as the Chishima Islands, triggering loud emergency alerts on millions of mobile phones. The JMA later clarified that a magnitude 6.9 quake had occurred near Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula at a depth of 160km just after midday.

items.title: Health Ministry: Over 6,700 officers approved for promotions and acting appointments, including four chopper crash victims
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — A total of 6,724 officers from various service schemes under the Ministry of Health (MOH) have been approved for acting appointments and promotions to the Senior Management Service (JUSA) and Grades 10 to 15. The move reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to recognise officers’ commitment, dedication and achievements in ensuring smooth operations and effective healthcare service delivery. In line with improvements to career progression under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), the board also approved excellence-based promotion criteria for officers under MOH’s teaching service scheme, allowing them to be promoted without a vacant post.

items.title: Four states exceed national drug involvement threshold
items.summary: MACHANG: Four states — Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu — have recorded drug involvement rates above the national threshold, with Pendang in Kedah and Kuala Krai in Kelantan emerging as the country's two highest-ranking districts. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the figures were calculated based on the number of people involved in drug cases per 100,000 population, using an international standard adopted by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC). Saifuddin said drug abuse among children below 15 was also becoming increasingly worrying, while those aged between 15 and 39 remained the largest group involved in drug abuse based on available profiles.

items.title: 75pct of prison inmates serving sentences for drug offences, says Saifuddin
items.summary: MACHANG: About 75 per cent of inmates in prisons nationwide are serving sentences for drug-related offences, with the proportion exceeding 90 per cent at Machang Prison, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said Malaysia had 41 prisons housing between 90,000 and 100,000 inmates, with drug-related offences accounting for the bulk of cases. On the Kampung Angkat Madani programme, Saifuddin said several projects had been implemented at Kampung Gosong to improve facilities and residents' well-being.

items.title: ‘That is not our job’: Amirudin rejects claims PKR plotted khalwat trap
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari today denied allegations that the party orchestrated a khalwat case involving former minister Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad to undermine a political rival. Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, said PKR had never discussed or arranged any plan, privately or publicly, to entrap political opponents, news outlet Harian Metro reported. The allegations surfaced after the Selangor Islamic Religious Department detained two people in Petaling Jaya last Thursday to assist investigations into a suspected khalwat offence.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected across country until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to affect parts of the country until 6pm. The same conditions were expected in several areas of Terengganu (Hulu Terengganu, Dungun, Kemaman, Besut and Setiu); Kelantan (Gua Musang, Jeli, Tanah Merah and Pasir Mas); Pahang (Bentong, Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Jerantut, Kuantan, Pekan, Rompin and Maran); and Negeri Sembilan (Jelebu, Seremban, Port Dickson, Rembau, Kuala Pilah and Tampin). In Sarawak, the affected areas were Kuching, Samarahan, Serian (Serian and Siburan), Sri Aman, Betong, Sarikei, Sibu (Sibu and Selangau), Mukah, Bintulu (Tatau), Kapit (Song), Miri and Limbang.

items.title: KL Immigration to probe alleged irregularities in special pass issuance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Kuala Lumpur Immigration Department will investigate allegations of irregularities in the issuance of special passes at the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Office. Its director, Datuk Hamsha Injau, said the department’s Integrity Division would conduct an investigation to determine the validity of the allegations and that no misconduct would be tolerated. He also advised the public to deal with the Immigration Department through official channels and avoid using unauthorised intermediaries.

items.title: N. Sembilan police: Post-mortem finds border agency officer died from pressure on neck, stab wounds
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 17 — Police said preliminary post-mortem findings showed that pressure applied to the neck caused the death of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer found at a government staff quarters in Nilai. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the finding followed a nearly five-hour post-mortem examination that began at 9.40 am today at Tuanku Ja’afar Hospital here. “The examination also found three stab wounds inflicted with a sharp weapon, two on the abdomen and one on the right cheek,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Melaka polls: PKR to field experienced, young and women candidates - Amirudin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PKR will field a mix of seasoned and experienced candidates, young people and women from various ethnic groups in the 16th Melaka state election on Nov 14. PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the party's candidates will be individuals capable of serving the community and possessing qualities that can help secure victory in the state constituencies they contest. PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said yesterday that the party would contest nine seats in the Melaka state election, with its list of candidates to be announced by PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also PH chairman, on Oct 24.

items.title: Malaysian Army to review SOP after serviceman arrested with pistol, ammunition and ketum, says chief
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Army (TDM) will review its standard operating procedures (SOP) following the arrest of a serviceman found with a pistol, dozens of rounds of ammunition and liquid suspected to be ketum at a camp in Kuala Lumpur. Chief of Army Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the review was part of the army’s continuous efforts to improve existing procedures and address any gaps identified. The event was also attended by Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.

items.title: Bersama suspends Nik Nazmi for 3 months over khalwat case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) has suspended its co-founder Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad from all official party activities for three months. Bersama president Syukri Razab said the party took note of Nik Nazmi's admission and viewed the matter seriously. He said issues involving party leaders and members must be addressed appropriately to safeguard the party's integrity, credibility and public confidence.

items.title: MAF reviewing allowances to boost reserve force participation, says Chief of Defence Force
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is reviewing allowances for its volunteer reserve personnel to encourage greater participation in training and strengthen the reserve force. Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the review was aimed at boosting commitment among reserve force members and strengthening the manpower pool for the regular armed forces. “Our target is a one-to-one ratio between reserve personnel and regular armed forces personnel,” he said.

items.title: Army to review SOP after personnel arrested with pistol, ammunition
items.summary: PORT DICKSON: The army will review its standard operating procedures (SOP) following the arrest of a serviceman found with a pistol, dozens of rounds of ammunition and liquid suspected to be ketum at a camp in Kuala Lumpur. Army chief Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the review was part of the army's continuous efforts to improve existing procedures and address any gaps identified. The event was also attended by Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.

items.title: Home minister: Immigration depots facing capacity pressure amid daily enforcement operations
items.summary: MACHANG, Oct 17 — Immigration depots nationwide are facing capacity pressures due to daily enforcement operations against undocumented migrants, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said. He said the depots had a combined capacity of about 20,000 people, but the continuous arrival of individuals detained during enforcement operations had led to overcrowding. The increase in detainees is also result of the Immigration Department’s mapping of areas with high concentrations of foreign nationals based on data collected and analysed from enforcement operations nationwide.

items.title: Police to complete probe involving MCBA chief after A-GC seeks improvements
items.summary: MACHANG: Police are completing their investigation into an incident involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 after the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) returned the investigation papers. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the A-GC requested several improvements to the investigation papers before deciding on the next course of action. "The police are still completing the investigation.

items.title: Six agencies swoop on Gombak premises, six Pakistanis detained
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Six Pakistanis were detained for suspected immigration offences during a multi-agency enforcement operation at two religious premises in Gombak, Selangor, yesterday. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the operation was coordinated by the Gombak district police headquarters and involved the police, Home Ministry, Immigration Department, Selayang Municipal Council, fire and rescue department and Registrar of Societies (ROS). Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said 76 people were brought to the Gombak district police headquarters for further checks following enforcement activities at a mosque in Kampung Nakhoda and another religious premises along Jalan Laksamana in Kampung Laksamana.

items.title: Sarawak election could be held as early as December
items.summary: KUCHING: The 13th Sarawak election could be held as early as December this year. Sarawak Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the dissolution of the state legislative assembly would ultimately depend on the decision of Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg. Karim said the current term of the Sarawak assembly would automatically expire in February 2027 after completing its five-year term.

items.title: Trump says Google rejected his idea to rename ocean after him
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Friday told supporters about his alleged attempt to have an ocean named after him and Google's refusal to go along with the idea, reported German news agency dpa. Speaking at a campaign rally in Georgia, Trump claimed he had suggested to representatives of the internet giant that either the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean be renamed the "Trump Ocean". Trump told supporters he had sent Google a map labelled "Trump Ocean", but company representatives rejected the idea.

items.title: Bersama suspends Nik Nazmi from party activities for three months from Oct 20 after Jais incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Parti Bersama Malaysia has suspended Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad from all official party activities for three months, effective October 20. “Bersama views this development seriously and takes the position that every issue involving the party’s leadership and members must be addressed appropriately to preserve the party’s integrity, credibility and public confidence,” Syukri Razab said in a statement on behalf of the party. The party stated that the decision was necessary and reasonable, without denying Nik Nazmi’s contributions and commitment to Bersama since the party was relaunched in May 2026.

items.title: Malaysia eyes bigger role in global maritime dispute resolution - Chief Justice
items.summary: He said Malaysia has long had a specialised Admiralty Court, and the establishment of the International Commercial and Admiralty Division (ICAD) has brought admiralty and international commercial cases under a single specialised division. Wan Ahmad Farid said that delays of even a few days in urgent admiralty cases could have significant commercial consequences, particularly when disputes involved vessels, cargo and parties across several jurisdictions. "Admiralty disputes are inherently international, involving vessel arrests, charterparty disputes, cargo claims, maritime security and arbitration.

items.title: Local cocoa production needs boost to cut import reliance
items.summary: MELAKA: Malaysia needs to boost local cocoa bean production to reduce reliance on imports, as the processing industry depends heavily on foreign supplies. Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad said stronger local production was needed to strengthen the cocoa supply chain and ensure growers benefited from the industry's expansion. However, growth in cocoa processing needed to be matched by higher local bean production so growers could also benefit, she said when opening A Malaysian Cocoa Affair 2026, organised by the Malaysian Cocoa Board (MCB) at a shopping centre in Banda Hilir today.

items.title: Drug abuse among Malaysian under-15s a growing concern, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: MACHANG, Oct 17 — The trend of drug abuse among those under the age of 15 is increasingly concerning and requires more comprehensive preventive efforts, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said that based on the profiles of individuals involved in drug abuse, those aged between 15 and 39 formed the largest group. Meanwhile, commenting on the seizure of 521 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine from a private jet in Laos recently, Saifuddin Nasution said the drugs were found aboard the aircraft before it was due to depart for Manila.

items.title: Lawyer: Zara Qairina’s mother yet to decide on civil action as inquest nears conclusion
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 17 — The legal team representing Noraidah Lamat, the mother of Zara Qairina Mahathir, has yet to decide whether to pursue civil action against any party, with its immediate focus on completing written submissions for the inquest. Counsel Shahlan Jufri, speaking on behalf of the team, said the matter would be discussed with Noraidah before any decision was made on further legal action. “For now, our focus is on the inquest, particularly the written submissions.

items.title: Man loses RM363,887 in alleged fake bank auction property scam in Miri
items.summary: MIRI, Oct 17 — A man who intended to buy a property for his family has allegedly been cheated out of RM363,887.49 in a non-existent bank auction property deal. Miri District Police Chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said in a statement shared on Miri police’s official social media page that the 56-year-old victim lodged a police report at Miri Central Police Station on October 15. “The suspect also offered to manage the purchase process, including the preparation of the Sales and Purchase Agreement (SPA) and property title transfer,” said the statement.

items.title: Transport minister: RM1,000 aid for remaining eligible taxi, rental car and school bus drivers to be paid via EFT
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — The remaining eligible taxi, rental car and school bus drivers nationwide will receive the RM1,000 Special Financial Aid directly into their respective bank accounts through Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT). Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the disbursement through this method would be carried out in the next phase, following the first phase of direct handovers to eligible drivers in several zones. “All the aid will be handed over to those who have been verified as eligible before Deepavali,” he told reporters after the special financial aid presentation ceremony for taxi, rental car and school bus drivers at Dewan Sri Pinang here today.

items.title: Malaysia records 5,278 domestic violence cases, with numbers still climbing, says Nancy Shukri (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 17 — A total of 5,278 domestic violence cases have been reported in Malaysia, with the number continuing to rise, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri. She said the ministry was placing greater emphasis on counselling and women’s empowerment to help women better understand their rights, build confidence and achieve financial independence. https://www.facebook.com/borneopost.online/videos/a-total-of-5278-domestic-violence-cases-have-been-reported-in-malaysia-with-the-/1385867886638367/ Commenting on the recent case in Negeri Sembilan involving a 35-year-old female customs officer who was allegedly murdered by her husband, Nancy said the ministry was looking into providing assistance to the victim’s family and children.

items.title: Sarawakian couple allegedly paid three friends RM8,000 each to smuggle cocaine into Japan, says Bukit Aman
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 17 — A Sarawakian husband and wife allegedly recruited three friends to traffic cocaine into Japan, said Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan. The Star reported that each of the three friends was paid RM8,000 and was believed to have known they were carrying contraband. Hussein said the couple had invited their three friends on what was presented as a holiday in Japan.

items.title: Ports, railways and highways could be next in Malaysia’s 5G coverage push
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Oct 17 — The Communications Ministry and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will study expanding telecommunications coverage targets, particularly for 5G, to include key economic areas such as ports, rail lines and highways. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the current Coverage of Populated Area (CoPA) metric should be reviewed to account for connectivity needs in areas with few or no residents but significant economic activity. “CoPA is frequently used by telecommunications companies and international bodies to refer to connectivity in populated areas.

items.title: Slain border agency officer’s remains to be buried in Tumpat tonight, says home minister
items.summary: MACHANG, Oct 17 — The remains of a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency officer allegedly killed by her husband in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, underwent a post-mortem this morning before being transported to Tumpat, Kelantan, for burial. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad reportedly said police received information about the incident at 8.30pm that day. Meanwhile, Kampung Gosong here has received RM500,000 to upgrade public facilities and residents’ homes under the ministry’s Kampung Angkat Madani initiative.

items.title: Motorists say RON95 wrecked their engines, and Selangor is now investigating seven petrol stations over watery fuel claims
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 17 — Selangor is investigating seven petrol stations after motorists complained that RON95 petrol suspected of being contaminated with water had damaged their vehicle engines, following similar allegations in northern states earlier this month. Selangor Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry director Muhamad Hanif Asa’ari said the ministry had received 10 official complaints involving the seven premises and collected 27 petrol samples for laboratory analysis. Earlier complaints in northern states Earlier this month, Penang’s Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry office reported receiving 33 complaints involving about 30 petrol stations over alleged water contamination in RON95.

items.title: Haze-hit areas: Parents to decide on childcare attendance, but kids must stay indoors, says family minister
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 17 — No taska (childcare centres) have been ordered to close so far due to the haze, but all outdoor activities must be suspended to reduce children’s exposure to polluted air. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the decision not to order a blanket closure of childcare centres took into account the needs of working parents who rely on the services. She said parents had the discretion to decide whether to send their children to childcare centres, particularly in areas where schools had been ordered to close following high Air Pollutant Index readings.

items.title: From neighbour disputes to legal reform, Malaysia moves to strengthen community mediation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Ministry of National Unity (KPN) is reviewing proposed improvements to the Mediation Act 2012 to establish a clearer legal framework for strengthening community mediation services under the National Unity and Integration Department (JPNIN). Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said the Act, which falls under the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU), does not specifically cover the operation of JPNIN’s community mediation services. He cited Singapore’s Community Mediation Centres Act 1997, India’s Mediation Act 2023 and Sri Lanka’s Mediation Boards Act 1988 as examples for comparison.
